ev.eth_m_injera.text: You sit by the hearth and watch the runny teff batter spread across the clay griddle and bubble with tiny holes. The first hot injera always goes to the children.
ev.eth_m_baptism.text: You were baptised {g:on the fortieth day, like every boy|on the eightieth day, like every girl}. The priest dipped you three times in the water, and a cord called a mateb was tied round your neck - the mark of a Christian for life.
ev.eth_m_timkat.text: At Timkat the priests carried the tabots down to the river under embroidered umbrellas. They sang by the water all night, and at dawn the water was blessed and the crowd splashed it over each other, laughing, as if baptised anew.
ev.eth_m_meskel.text: At Meskel the whole village built a huge bonfire decked with the yellow daisies that bloom after the rains. When it collapsed, the old people watched which way the top fell: they say it tells what kind of year is coming.
ev.eth_m_fast.text: It is the Great Lent: fifty-five days without meat, milk or butter, and no food before noon. Altogether there are more than two hundred fasting days a year - and your stomach never quite gets used to it.
ev.eth_m_fasika.text: On Easter night, after the long service, the fast ended at first cockcrow. The chicken in thick spiced sauce, simmering since the evening, tasted like the best food in the world.
ev.eth_m_bete_giyorgis.text: For the first time you peered into the deep pit at the bottom of which stands the church of Saint George - cut from a single block of rock in the shape of a cross. They say angels carried on the work at night while people slept.
ev.eth_m_aksum_stelae.text: Outside the town lies a broken stele longer than any house. The old men say the ancient kings raised it by the power of the Ark. You walked its length - forty paces from end to end.
ev.eth_m_aksum_women.text: Women are not allowed into the precinct of Mary of Zion - they pray at the outer wall. You watched the men go in and thought that the Virgin Mary was a woman too.
ev.eth_m_shamma.text: You threw on a new white shamma with a coloured border. The cloth smells of cotton and hearth smoke, and the folds fall over your shoulder the way the nobles wear it.
ev.eth_m_hyenas.text: At night the hyenas cackle by the pen. The cattle press against the wall, the dogs bark themselves hoarse, and you lie under a sheepskin counting to a hundred so as not to be afraid.
ev.eth_m_kiremt.text: The great rains have come. The rivers are swollen, the roads washed out, and until Meskel nobody goes further than the next village. Time to mend tools, spin and tell stories by the fire.
ev.eth_m_tej.text: At a neighbour's wedding they served tej - honey wine, golden and treacherous. After the third horn you sang louder than anyone, and you still cannot remember what.
ev.eth_m_genna.text: At Genna, the Christmas feast, the young men of two villages chased a wooden ball with crooked sticks until dark. You came home with a split knee, very proud of yourself.
ev.eth_m_zema.text: In church the debteras sang the ancient chant: sistrums jingled, the drum beat slowly, prayer staffs swayed. You did not understand a word of Ge'ez, but it gave you goosebumps.
ev.eth_m_mahber.text: It was your turn to host the mahber, the brotherhood of Saint Michael. The neighbours gathered, the priest blessed the bread and you fed everyone until dark. Costly - but now you truly belong.
ev.eth_m_amole.text: At the weekly market everything is counted in bars of salt. The trader turned your bar over and over, tapped it on a stone and announced that a corner was chipped - so it was worth less.
ev.eth_m_camels.text: A caravan came up from the lowlands: camels loaded with salt and cloth, and drivers speaking a strange tongue. The children ran after them all the way to the market.
ev.eth_m_jugol.text: You walked the city wall from gate to gate. They say Emir Nur built it so that Harar would never be burned again.
ev.eth_m_khat.text: After the noon prayer you sit on the rugs with the neighbours, slowly chewing khat leaves. The conversation grows long and the arguments soft.
ev.eth_m_coffee.text: Coffee beans are roasting on a clay pan, and the smell drifts down the whole lane. They say the Sufis drink this bitter brew to stay awake through the night prayers.
ev.eth_m_tana.text: On the road you saw the falls people call "smoking water": the Abay - the Blue Nile - plunges off the cliffs in a cloud of spray. On Lake Tana fishermen paddle boats of bound papyrus.
ev.eth_m_herding.text: You have been trusted to herd the goats on the hillside. You learned to sling a stone straight and to whistle so that the goats come running to the sound.
ev.eth_m_plough.text: For the first time you guided the maresha plough behind a pair of oxen on your own. The furrow came out as crooked as a snake, but the old men said everyone starts that way.
ev.eth_m_spinning.text: You have been taught to spin cotton: the spindle twirls and the thread draws out finer and finer. While their hands are busy, the women share the best gossip in the village.
ev.eth_m_amba_geshen.text: In the distance rises Amba Geshen, a flat-topped mountain with sheer sides. The king's kinsmen are kept there under guard so they cannot fight over the throne. They say many grow old up there without ever coming down.
ev.eth_m_sabbath.text: At sunset on Friday the Beta Israel community washed and fell quiet: the Sabbath had come. No fire, no work - only prayers and stillness until the next evening.
ev.eth_m_ramadan.text: The month of Ramadan: by day the streets are empty and quiet, and after sunset they fill with the smell of food and the sound of voices. You wait all day for evening.
ev.eth_m_old_tales.text: The neighbours' children gather round you in the evenings: tell us again about King Lalibela, whose cradle was swarmed by bees. You tell it - and believe it a little more each time.
ev.eth_m_qene.text: The teacher explains qene verse: each one has "wax" - what is said - and "gold" - what is hidden inside. You composed your first couplet, and the teacher grunted almost approvingly.
ev.eth_m_st_george.text: On the church wall Saint George on a white horse spears the serpent. All the saints have huge eyes that look straight at you wherever you stand.
ev.eth_m_slave_song.text: Sometimes in your sleep you hear a song in a language you have almost forgotten - a song from the southern lands you were taken from as a child. In the morning only the tune remains.
ev.eth_m_royal_camp.text: The royal camp passed through the valley: thousands of tents, mules, soldiers, priests carrying tabots, drums. Next morning there was only a trampled field where it had stood - and empty granaries in the village.
ev.eth_m_debre_damo.text: You climbed a rope up the sheer cliff to the monastery of Debre Damo. No women are allowed there, not even female animals - only men. From the top you can see half the world.
ev.eth_church_school.title: Church school
ev.eth_church_school.text: The priest of the next church is taking pupils. First the fidel alphabet, then the whole Psalter by heart, under a tree by the churchyard wall. The teacher must be paid in grain, and the fields will lose a pair of hands.
ev.eth_church_school_later.title: The Psalter by heart
ev.eth_church_school_later.text: You know the whole Psalter by heart, from the first psalm to the last. The priest says it is time to choose: become a deacon and go on to the schools of chant and qene - or go back to the plough.
ev.eth_gult_dues.title: Dues to the lord
ev.eth_gult_dues.text: The gult holder's man has come for the dues: a share of the grain, honey, and a week of work on the lord's field - just as your own teff is ripe.
ev.eth_gult_dues.haggle.success: You settled on half. The lord's man left grumbling.
ev.eth_gult_dues.haggle.failure: He lost his temper and took more than he first asked.
ev.eth_gult_dues.elders.success: The elders agreed that custom allows no such demand. The dues were cut.
ev.eth_gult_dues.elders.failure: The complaint reached the lord, and he did not forget it.
ev.eth_rist_claim.title: A rist dispute
ev.eth_rist_claim.text: A distant kinsman claims a share of the family land. Rist passes down through both the father's and the mother's line, but the only proof is to name all your ancestors before the elders - one by one, seven generations back.
ev.eth_rist_claim.recite.success: You named them all without a single slip. The elders nodded, and the kinsman left empty-handed.
ev.eth_rist_claim.recite.failure: You stumbled at the fifth generation. Part of the land went to the kinsman.
ev.eth_rist_claim.bribe.success: The gifts did their work. The land stayed yours.
ev.eth_rist_claim.bribe.failure: The bribe came out, and the whole district talked of nothing else.
ev.eth_rist_claim_later.title: A debt of kinship
ev.eth_rist_claim_later.text: The kinsman you once shared the land with came of his own accord in a hard year, bringing oxen for the ploughing and a sack of grain. "The land remembers how it was shared," he said.
ev.eth_billeting.title: Billeted soldiers
ev.eth_billeting.text: A troop of royal soldiers has come to the village. Custom says they must be fed and given drink until they leave - and they are in no hurry, and are already eyeing your granary.
ev.eth_billeting.hide: Hide the grain in a pit
ev.eth_billeting.hide.success: The soldiers left without finding the cache.
ev.eth_billeting.hide.failure: They found the pit. They took everything, and you took a beating too.
ev.eth_billeting.complain.success: The commander turned out to have a conscience and reined in his men.
ev.eth_billeting.complain.failure: The commander just laughed, and the soldiers took even more.
ev.eth_qurban.title: A church wedding
ev.eth_qurban.text: Your marriage is an ordinary semanya contract - the way almost everyone in the village marries, and it can be dissolved. {npc} wants to be wed in church with communion - a qurban marriage. After that there can never be a divorce.
ev.eth_godparent.title: Godparent
ev.eth_godparent.text: The neighbours ask you to be godparent to their newborn. It is no small thing: a godparent here is almost family, for life, with all the feasts, troubles and gifts that go with it.
ev.eth_jerusalem.title: The road to Jerusalem
ev.eth_jerusalem.text: Pilgrims are gathering for Jerusalem, where Ethiopian monks keep their own cells by the Holy Sepulchre. The road is long: across the desert, through Egypt and the lands of Muslim sultans. Not everyone comes back.
ev.eth_jerusalem.go.success: You stood at the Holy Sepulchre and came home a different person.
ev.eth_jerusalem.go.failure: You fell gravely ill in the desert and barely made it home without ever reaching the city.
ev.eth_jerusalem_later.title: "Tell us about Jerusalem"
ev.eth_jerusalem_later.text: Years have passed, but people still invite you in the evenings: tell us about Jerusalem, the Holy Sepulchre, the Egyptian merchants and the sea of sand. Your pilgrimage has become a story people retell even without you.
ev.eth_monastery_call.title: The call of the monastery
ev.eth_monastery_call.text: An old acquaintance has entered a monastery on the mountain and sent word: there is silence here, prayer and a peace that does not exist below. Many people your age leave everything and go. Perhaps it is your time too?
ev.eth_fast_illness.title: Sick during the fast
ev.eth_fast_illness.text: You are ill, and it is a fasting season. The healer tells you to eat meat and drink milk to get your strength back. The priest frowns: the sick may be excused, but it would be better if you endured.
ev.eth_fast_illness.break: Eat meat as the healer says
ev.eth_fast_illness.break.success: Your strength returned and the illness passed.
ev.eth_fast_illness.break.failure: The meat did not help, and your conscience nags you.
ev.eth_fast_illness.keep.success: You held out - and the illness went away by itself.
ev.eth_holy_water.title: Holy water
ev.eth_holy_water.text: You have been ill for weeks. The neighbours say to go to the holy spring at the monastery: for seven days they pour water over you and pray. The healer offers cautery and bitter herbs.
ev.eth_holy_water.tsebel.success: On the sixth day the fever broke. You walked home on your own feet.
ev.eth_holy_water.tsebel.failure: The cold water and the long road only drained your strength.
ev.eth_holy_water.healer.failure: The cautery hurt, and did no good.
ev.eth_holy_water.rest.success: The illness passed on its own.
ev.eth_mahber_join.title: The brotherhood
ev.eth_mahber_join.text: The neighbours invite you into a mahber, a brotherhood dedicated to a saint. Once a month they meet, pray, eat and help each other in hard times. Each member hosts the meal in turn, and it is not cheap.
ev.eth_mahber_later.title: Brothers of the mahber
ev.eth_mahber_later.text: When trouble came, your mahber brothers did not forget you: they brought grain, ploughed your field and sat with you until morning. All those monthly meals came back a hundredfold.
ev.eth_oath.title: An oath before the tabot
ev.eth_oath.text: A neighbour insists you owe him two oxen. There are no witnesses. The elders propose settling it with an oath in church before the tabot: whoever lies, they say, God will punish.
ev.eth_oath.swear.success: You swore without a tremor, and the neighbour backed down.
ev.eth_oath.swear.failure: Your voice wavered treacherously, and the elders decided against you.
ev.eth_oath.accuse.success: You reminded everyone of his past tricks, and he dropped the claim himself.
ev.eth_oath.accuse.failure: The accusation failed. Now you have an enemy - and a debt.
ev.eth_confessor.title: Father of the soul
ev.eth_confessor.text: In noble houses everyone has a "father of the soul", a confessor whose advice guides every decision. You are offered two: a stern monk from a mountain monastery and a cheerful priest from the next church.
ev.eth_buy_captive.title: A merchant from the south
ev.eth_buy_captive.text: A merchant has brought a boy taken from the southern lands and offers to sell him. The boy says nothing and stares at the floor. In wealthy houses this is common enough, but that does not make it easier.
ev.eth_buy_captive.free: Buy him and set him free
ev.eth_buda_rumor.title: The evil eye
ev.eth_buda_rumor.text: After a child died in the village, whispers began: it was the potter woman at the edge of the village - she is a buda, they say, with the evil eye. Craftsfolk are shunned as it is, and now people want to drive her out.
ev.eth_leopard.title: Leopard
ev.eth_leopard.text: In the night a leopard got into the pen and carried off a goat. Towards dawn it came back: you can see its eyes glowing by the fence.
ev.eth_leopard.spear.success: The beast slunk off snarling and never came back. The whole village is talking about you.
ev.eth_leopard.spear.failure: The leopard sprang at you. You will carry the scars for life.
ev.eth_leopard.fire: Make noise and keep the fire going until dawn
ev.eth_blood_feud.title: Blood feud
ev.eth_blood_feud.text: A man of your kin killed a neighbour in a quarrel. Now the dead man's family demands blood - or a price paid in cattle and salt. The elders are waiting to hear what you say.
ev.eth_blood_feud.pay: Pay your share of the blood price
ev.eth_blood_feud.church: Ask a priest to reconcile the families
ev.eth_blood_feud.church.success: The priest talked both sides round. The price was set fairly.
ev.eth_blood_feud.church.failure: There was no peace, and you paid more in the end.
ev.eth_blood_feud_later.title: Not forgotten
ev.eth_blood_feud_later.text: Years have passed, but the dead man's kin have not forgotten. On the road three men with spears stopped you and said the time had come.
ev.eth_blood_feud_later.fight.success: You beat them off and they backed away. But the blood between the families remains.
ev.eth_blood_feud_later.fight.failure: You were badly wounded and left by the road.
ev.eth_blood_feud_later.sanctuary.succes: Inside the churchyard nobody touched you. The priest took on the task of making peace.
ev.eth_blood_feud_later.sanctuary.failur: You reached the church, but not unhurt.
ev.eth_debo.title: Debo
ev.eth_debo.text: A neighbour calls for a debo, a work party: the whole village will bring in his harvest before the rains. No pay, only food and tej in the evening - and your own field is waiting too.
ev.eth_debo_later.title: Your debo
ev.eth_debo_later.text: The year you fell ill right at harvest time, the whole village turned out on your field. You once helped them - and they remembered.
ev.eth_locusts.title: Locusts
ev.eth_locusts.text: The southern sky has darkened and begun to hum: locusts are coming. Within the hour they will be on your field.
ev.eth_locusts.smoke.failure: The smoke did nothing: only stalks were left.
ev.eth_locusts.reap: Reap it unripe while you can
ev.eth_locusts.pray.success: The locusts passed you by. The priest said your prayers were heard.
ev.eth_locusts.pray.failure: While you prayed, the locusts ate everything.
ev.eth_gugs.title: Gugs
ev.eth_gugs.text: At the feast the young nobles are playing gugs: horsemen charge at each other hurling blunt javelins, and the target ducks behind a round shield. They call you into the game.
ev.eth_gugs.play.success: You took no hits and landed three. Every girl was watching you.
ev.eth_gugs.play.failure: A javelin caught your shoulder and you flew out of the saddle.
ev.eth_fetha_negest.title: The Law of Kings
ev.eth_fetha_negest.text: Before you is a case of cattle theft. The elders judge by custom: repay twice over and make peace. But learned priests have brought the Fetha Negest, the "Law of Kings", a book translated from Arabic, which prescribes something else.
ev.eth_fetha_negest.reconcile: Persuade both sides to make peace
ev.eth_fetha_negest.reconcile.success: Both sides left satisfied - a rare thing.
ev.eth_fetha_negest.reconcile.failure: There was no peace, and you were called indecisive.
ev.eth_zeila_caravan.title: A caravan to the sea
ev.eth_zeila_caravan.text: A great caravan is leaving for the sea at Zeila: coffee, hides, musk and wax going out; cloth, dates, iron and dishes from across the sea coming back. You can buy a share or go yourself.
ev.eth_zeila_caravan.go.success: You came back with a good profit and the dust of every road on your clothes.
ev.eth_zeila_caravan.go.failure: The caravan was attacked in the desert. The goods were lost and you barely survived.
ev.eth_zeila_caravan_later.title: The caravan is back
ev.eth_zeila_caravan_later.text: The caravan from Zeila has returned, and your share has turned into bales of cloth and a fine profit. The merchants in the bazaar now greet you first.
ev.eth_f_sabbath.title: Two Sabbaths
ev.eth_f_sabbath.text: A monk of the community of Ewostatewos's disciples says God gave two Sabbaths - the Sabbath of the Old Testament and Sunday - and both must be honoured. The bishop allows only Sunday, and those who keep both are driven from the churches.
ev.eth_f_sabbath.note: The monk Ewostatewos (c. 1273–1352) taught that both Saturday and Sunday should be kept holy. His followers were persecuted for decades until the Council of Debre Mitmaq under Zara Yaqob (1450) accepted both Sabbaths.
ev.eth_f_stephanites.title: Visitors in the night
ev.eth_f_stephanites.text: In the night Stephanite monks knocked at your door. They refuse to bow before icons of the Virgin or before the king himself, and Zara Yaqob has ordered them hunted down. They ask you to hide them until morning.
ev.eth_f_stephanites.hide.success: At dawn they left for the mountains, blessing your house.
ev.eth_f_stephanites.hide.failure: Someone informed. You had to pay and explain yourself to the governor's men.
ev.eth_f_stephanites.note: The followers of the monk Estifanos (15th century) refused to bow to icons and to the king. Zara Yaqob persecuted them harshly; later the community was reconciled with the church.
ev.eth_f_land_baptism.title: Land for baptism
ev.eth_f_land_baptism.text: A royal word has been proclaimed: whoever is baptised shall inherit the land of their fathers, and whoever is not shall go landless. Your Christian neighbours urge you: be baptised and it will all be yours. The elders of the community say nothing and watch you.
ev.eth_f_land_baptism.outward: Be baptised for show and pray the old way
ev.eth_f_land_baptism.keep: Stay in the faith of the Beta Israel
ev.eth_f_land_baptism.note: Tradition credits King Yeshaq (1414–1429) with a decree: "He who is baptised may inherit the land of his father; otherwise let him be landless." Measures like this cost many Beta Israel their land and pushed them into crafts. The exact wording is disputed.
ev.eth_f_slave_baptism.title: Baptism
ev.eth_f_slave_baptism.text: The lady of the house wants you baptised. By custom a baptised servant is not sold to Muslim traders, and the household will call you by a Christian name. But you remember the gods and ancestors of your childhood.
ev.eth_f_slave_baptism.refuse: Ask to keep your own faith
ev.eth_f_meat.title: Another's meat
ev.eth_f_meat.text: A Muslim merchant invites you to share his meal. But Christians do not eat meat slaughtered by a Muslim, and Muslims do not eat meat slaughtered by a Christian. Everyone knows this - and yet a refusal is an insult.
ev.eth_f_meat.bread: Eat only bread and honey, and praise the meat
ev.eth_f_oromo_feast.title: An Oromo feast
ev.eth_f_oromo_feast.text: The Oromo now live in the next valley. Their elders pray to Waaqa, the sky god, beneath a great tree, and every eight years power passes to a new generation of men - that is their gada system. An Oromo acquaintance invites you to a feast.
ev.eth_f_baptize_south.title: Monks with a cross
ev.eth_f_baptize_south.text: Monks from a great monastery go from village to village baptising in the river. The clan elders are against it: the ancestors will be offended and the land will stop bearing. The monk promises you the church's protection and a place among Christians.
ev.eth_f_baptize_south.ancestors: Keep the faith of your ancestors
ev.eth_f_jesuit.title: A learned Frank
ev.eth_f_jesuit.text: A Jesuit monk from the distant land of the Franks speaks pure Ge'ez and argues about the nature of Christ better than any debtera. King Susenyos himself listens to him. He urges you to accept the Roman faith.
ev.eth_f_jesuit.refuse: Keep the faith of your fathers
ev.eth_f_jesuit.note: The Spanish Jesuit Pedro Páez (in Ethiopia from 1603) learned Ge'ez and Amharic and persuaded King Susenyos (1607–1632) to become a Catholic; the king declared it publicly in 1622.
ev.eth_f_jesuit_later.title: The wind has changed
ev.eth_f_jesuit_later.text: Many grumble against the Roman faith: the priests call people back to the faith of their fathers, and the neighbours eye you and whisper "Frank". They say things may change at court as well.
ev.eth_f_harar_convert.title: The shahada
ev.eth_f_harar_convert.text: You have lived in Harar among Muslims for a long time. A friend invites you to the mosque: say the shahada - "there is no god but God" - and you will be one of them here.
ev.eth_t_king_notice.title: The negus's eye
ev.eth_t_king_notice.text: The royal camp halted by your village. At the review you caught the eye of the negus himself - and said something that made him laugh. Next morning a messenger came: the king wants you at court.
ev.eth_t_king_notice_later.title: Disgrace
ev.eth_t_king_notice_later.text: Your patron at court has fallen from favour: he is accused of conspiring with rebels. Those who sought his friendship yesterday now walk round his tent.
ev.eth_t_king_notice_later.loyal.success: The charges melted away, and your patron did not forget who stood by him.
ev.eth_t_king_notice_later.loyal.failure: He fell, and you fell with him.
ev.eth_t_captured.title: Raiders
ev.eth_t_captured.text: Slave raiders fell on you on the road. The bound captives are being driven down to the lowlands, where caravans leave for the sea.
ev.eth_t_captured.escape.success: At night you wore through the rope on a rock and made your way home through the mountains.
ev.eth_t_captured.escape.failure: They caught you. The road home is closed.
ev.eth_t_captured.plead.success: Your family scraped together the ransom - nearly everything they had.
ev.eth_t_ransomed.title: Ransomed
ev.eth_t_ransomed.text: Monks from a monastery ransomed several Christian captives from the coastal traders. Your name was on the list. The road home took a month, but every step was light.
ev.eth_t_gult_grant.title: A royal gult
ev.eth_t_gult_grant.text: For loyal service the king grants you a gult - the right to collect dues from three villages. The villages are far away, and their former holder will hardly be pleased to see them go to an upstart.
ev.eth_t_buda_accused.title: Accused
ev.eth_t_buda_accused.text: The headman's child fell gravely ill, and the healer declared it was the evil eye - and that the eye was yours. Smiths and potters are feared as it is, and now the neighbours clench their fists when you pass.
ev.eth_t_buda_accused.church.success: The priest took your arm in front of everyone and led you into church. The whispers died down.
ev.eth_t_buda_accused.church.failure: The priest did not want to quarrel with the village.
ev.eth_t_buda_accused.endure: Endure it and wait for them to forget
ev.eth_t_ancient_gold.title: Ancient gold
ev.eth_t_ancient_gold.text: Ploughing the field, you turned up a clay pot full of small gold coins stamped with crosses and the faces of kings nobody remembers. No such money has been struck here for centuries.
ev.eth_t_ancient_gold.church: Take it to the church of Mary of Zion
ev.eth_t_ancient_gold.sell: Sell it secretly to Arab merchants
ev.eth_t_ancient_gold.sell.success: The merchants gave you more salt than you had seen in your whole life.
ev.eth_t_ancient_gold.sell.failure: The lord learned of the find. The gold was taken and you were punished.
ev.eth_t_ancient_gold.hide: Hide it and spend a little at a time
ev.eth_t_salt_flats.title: The salt flats
ev.eth_t_salt_flats.text: A merchant is looking for someone to lead a great caravan to the salt flats in the lowlands: it is an inferno down there, water is worth a life, and the nomads charge for every well. Come back, and your share will be like nothing you have ever had.
ev.eth_t_salt_flats.lead.success: You brought the caravan home without loss. The mules sag under salt bars - and some of them are yours.
ev.eth_t_salt_flats.lead.failure: The heat felled you halfway. They brought you home on a mule, with no share and no strength.
ev.eth_t_lord_rebels.title: Rebellion
ev.eth_t_lord_rebels.text: Your lord has risen against the king and calls everyone who owes him service to his banner. The royal army is already on the march, and neither side will let you sit it out.
ev.eth_t_lord_rebels.follow.success: The king chose to make peace with the rebel, and his men were rewarded.
ev.eth_t_lord_rebels.follow.failure: The rebellion was crushed. You are in hiding, having lost almost everything.
ev.eth_t_lord_rebels.betray.failure: Your lord's men found out about the message before the king did.
ev.eth_t_moggaasaa.title: New neighbours
ev.eth_t_moggaasaa.text: The Oromo have taken the valley. Some neighbours fled to the mountains, others stayed - and the Oromo elders adopt them into their clans through the rite of moggaasaa. A new clan member gets a name and protection. You are offered the same.
ev.eth_t_moggaasaa.stay: Stay, but live your own way
ev.eth_t_dejazmach_match.title: A dejazmach's matchmakers
ev.eth_t_dejazmach_match.text: A powerful dejazmach sends matchmakers: he wants a marriage alliance through {npc}. You never dared dream of such a match. But the dejazmach has many enemies at court.
ev.eth_t_dejazmach_fall.title: Disfavour
ev.eth_t_dejazmach_fall.text: The dejazmach you married into has fallen from favour: the king ordered him chained and sent to a mountain prison. The shadow has fallen on your house too.
ev.eth_t_dejazmach_fall.plead: Ride to court to plead for him
ev.eth_t_dejazmach_fall.plead.success: The king relented. Your name stayed clean.
ev.eth_t_dejazmach_fall.plead.failure: You were not even admitted to the king.
ev.eth_t_dejazmach_fall.lie_low: Lie low and wait it out
ev.eth_t_emir_treasury.title: The emir's treasury
ev.eth_t_emir_treasury.text: The emir has noticed your skill in business and offers you a place at the treasury, reckoning taxes and caravan tolls. Honour, income - and plenty of envy.
ev.eth_t_portuguese.title: The Portuguese
ev.eth_t_portuguese.text: One of the Portuguese who stayed on after the war with the imam has settled nearby and married a local woman. He mends muskets, forges in the Frankish way and offers you a share. The priests look askance at "Franks", but he pays well.
ev.eth_t_portuguese.join.success: You picked up the Frankish techniques quickly, and customers began coming to you.
ev.eth_t_portuguese.join.failure: The neighbours started whispering that you had sold yourself to the Franks.
ev.eth_w_debtera_scroll.title: A healing scroll
ev.eth_w_debtera_scroll.text: A woman asks you to write a healing scroll: Ge'ez prayers and wide-eyed angels on a strip of parchment as long as she is tall. The priests grumble that debteras come too close to sorcery.
ev.eth_w_debtera_qene.title: Qene at the feast
ev.eth_w_debtera_qene.text: At a great feast it falls to you to compose a qene before the whole assembly - "wax and gold", a double meaning in every word. A noble guest clearly expects to be praised.
ev.eth_w_debtera_qene.barb.success: Those who understood laughed for a long time, and the guest noticed nothing.
ev.eth_w_debtera_qene.barb.failure: The guest understood everything. Now you have a powerful enemy.
ev.eth_w_monk_hermit.title: A cave above the abyss
ev.eth_w_monk_hermit.text: The elder suggests you go further - to a cave above a precipice where hermits live. Food every second day, a word once a week. They say only there can God truly be heard.
ev.eth_w_monk_gospel.title: A Gospel for a new church
ev.eth_w_monk_gospel.text: The monastery has decided to copy a Gospel book on parchment for a new church. It is a year's work: soot ink, a reed pen, and the miniatures of the Evangelists are your task.
ev.eth_w_icon_commission.title: A Virgin for the lady
ev.eth_w_icon_commission.text: A noble lady commissions an icon of the Virgin and Child for her church. Since the days of King Zara Yaqob the Virgin Mary has been honoured here above all saints, and the lady wants an icon worthy of the feast.
ev.eth_w_icon_frank.title: A Frankish painter
ev.eth_w_icon_frank.text: A Venetian works at court; here they call him Marqorewos. His saints look alive, with shadows on their faces, and his Virgin holds the Child the way real children are held. You could ask to become his pupil.
ev.eth_w_coffee_lot.title: A big harvest
ev.eth_w_coffee_lot.text: The gardeners have brought in a big coffee harvest, and the caravan to the sea will not leave for a month. You could buy it all cheaply - if the beans don't get damp and the caravan isn't delayed.
ev.eth_w_coffee_lot.all.success: The caravan left on time, and in Zeila the beans sold for three times the price.
ev.eth_w_coffee_lot.all.failure: Half the sacks went damp. You barely got your money back.
ev.eth_w_salt_heat.title: The short cut
ev.eth_w_salt_heat.text: On the salt flats it is so hot the stones crack. An Afar guide offers a short cut across a waterless basin - two days faster. The long road passes the wells, but there are tolls to pay.
ev.eth_w_salt_heat.short.success: You reached the market first and sold your salt dearer than anyone.
ev.eth_w_salt_heat.short.failure: The water ran out on the second day. You barely made it alive.
ev.eth_w_carver_crack.title: A crack in the rock
ev.eth_w_carver_crack.text: Halfway through the work a crack opened in the rock - right where a pillar is meant to stand. The master says to pray and keep cutting. But you can see the pillar may collapse.
ev.eth_w_carver_crack.redesign: Persuade the master to move the pillar
ev.eth_w_carver_crack.redesign.success: The master agreed. The pillar stands in its new place, as solid as the mountain.
ev.eth_w_carver_crack.redesign.failure: The master sent you to do menial work for your cheek.
ev.eth_w_carver_crack.continue.success: The crack held. The master paid generously.
ev.eth_w_carver_crack.continue.failure: A slab of rock fell right on you.
ev.eth_w_beta_spears.title: A hundred spearheads
ev.eth_w_beta_spears.text: A Christian lord orders a hundred spearheads from you. He pays well. But they say the spears will be used against the rebels in the Semien mountains, where your fellow believers live.
ev.eth_w_beta_spears.refuse.success: The lord shrugged and found another smith.
ev.eth_w_beta_spears.refuse.failure: The lord was furious: you were beaten and your tools were taken.
ev.eth_w_chronicle.title: Chronicle of a defeat
ev.eth_w_chronicle.text: The king lost a battle but ordered the chronicle to say the enemy fled in terror. The scribe before you wrote the truth - and now lives in exile on a mountain.
ev.eth_w_chronicle.subtle: Write it so the wise will see the truth
ev.eth_w_chronicle.subtle.success: The king was pleased, and posterity will read between the lines.
ev.eth_w_chronicle.subtle.failure: A clever courtier understood everything and informed on you.
ev.eth_w_scribe_azaj.title: Azaj
ev.eth_w_scribe_azaj.text: Your charters and chronicles have pleased the court. The king appoints you azaj - steward of the camp's affairs: justice, supplies, land charters.
ev.eth_w_soldier_fitawrari.title: First into the enemy camp
ev.eth_w_soldier_fitawrari.text: In battle you were the first to break into the enemy camp. Now the king wants to make you fitawrari, leader of the vanguard.
ev.eth_w_forge_own.title: A forge of your own
ev.eth_w_forge_own.text: The old master is nearly blind and wants to hand you his forge - bellows, anvil and orders from the church. In return you must give him part of your income for the rest of his days.
ev.eth_w_salt_partner.title: Caravans of your own
ev.eth_w_salt_partner.text: You know every well on the salt road. A merchant offers to make you his partner: enough leading other men's caravans - time for your own.
ev.eth_w_steward.title: The storeroom keys
ev.eth_w_steward.text: The old steward has died, and the lady of the house wants to entrust the household to you: the keys to the stores of teff and honey, the servants, the dealings with traders.
ev.eth_w_priest_tabot.title: A new tabot
ev.eth_w_priest_tabot.text: Your church's tabot - the altar tablet without which no service can be held - has cracked. Only the abun can consecrate a new one, and there is just one for the whole country, travelling with the royal camp.
ev.eth_w_priest_tabot.wait: Wait until the abun comes near
ev.eth_w_imam_dispute.title: An inheritance dispute
ev.eth_w_imam_dispute.text: Two men have come to the mosque: by sharia an orphan is owed a share, but the uncle has already taken the garden. Everyone is waiting for your word.
ev.eth_w_imam_dispute.mercy: Persuade the uncle to yield kindly
ev.eth_mv_camp.title: With the royal camp
ev.eth_mv_camp.text: They say the royal camp in Shewa always needs hands: smiths, drovers, bakers, porters. There is pay there - and everything is decided there.
ev.eth_mv_aksum.title: Closer to the Ark
ev.eth_mv_aksum.text: You have long dreamed of living near Aksum and the church of Mary of Zion, where the Ark is kept. A priest you know promises to help you settle there.
ev.eth_mv_harar.title: To Harar
ev.eth_mv_harar.text: Harar is growing: Muslim merchants from all over the highlands are moving there. Mosques, markets, brothers in faith - and nobody looks at you askance in the bazaar.
ev.eth_mv_lalibela.title: A new Jerusalem
ev.eth_mv_lalibela.text: Pilgrims call Lalibela a new Jerusalem: it has its own Golgotha and its own Jordan. Many come to pray and stay for good beside the rock churches.
ev.eth_mv_from_harar.title: Home to the highlands
ev.eth_mv_from_harar.text: There are few Christians in Harar, and life is not easy for them. Caravan men say they can take you up to the highlands, to Shewa, where church gongs ring and Meskel is celebrated.
